transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Jules Kim, Ava Rodriguez (Redwood) — Maya Thompson, Diego Rivera, Priya Nair, Ethan Cole, Zoe Park (Lyra)
Recording id: lyra-2026-03-22-rc1

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do a quick round robin and then we can jump into the postmortem follow-up, are we all good on time?
[00:12] Maya: yes thanks Samir, short on time but we really want to make sure we have the mitigations lined up.
[00:20] Jules: hi everybody, i'll start with a super quick recap of what we found in the initial RCA — feel free to jump in, i know some of the wording in the doc was a bit fuzzy.

[00:32] Jules: so the outage on 2026-03-15 was triggered when our serving autoscaler attempted to rebalance GPU capacity during a sudden traffic spike. there was an interaction with prefix / KV cache eviction — we sometimes saw large eviction storms when many requests had long context lengths which caused downstream latency spikes and then the autoscaler to spin up ephemeral nodes. the sequence we think is: cache eviction -> cold KV miss -> longer tail latency -> autoscaler adds nodes -> redispatch leads to transient load on the control plane -> additional latencies and retries, which amplified the issue.
[01:10] Diego: yeah, to add — we saw a very tight race window where the autoscaler policy's cooldown was too short and it launched many small allocations rather than a few bigger ones. that increased scheduling churn on our cluster. also, some of our VM preemption logic caused pods to be rescheduled in ways that didn't preserve warm KV caches.
[01:32] Maya: and just to be clear, the outage impacted the clinical data ingestion pipeline and a couple of user-facing features for about 18 minutes at peak. not catastrophic but enough to trigger pagers and a customer-facing incident.

[01:50] Samir: thanks — quick note: some of the transcriptions in the doc say 'KV cash' or 'K V cache' so we cleaned that up. also there was a mention of 'Redwood Dedicated' — for clarity the Dedicated pool we suggested is the same config that we used in the emergency mitigation.
[02:08] Ethan: on security side we want to confirm that audit logs were intact during the window and there was no data exfil. we saw normal access patterns.

[02:25] Ava: ok short-term mitigations we applied: 1) sticky allocation rule so that hot prefixes stay on pinned GPUs for 15 minutes; 2) increased KV cache size threshold to reduce eviction storms; 3) adjusted the autoscaler cooldown from 30s to 90s and increased minimum burst allocation; 4) turned on request-level circuit breaker to fail-fast for heavy long-context requests so we don't cascade. those were rolled within the emergency window and we monitored.
[03:05] Zoe: quick question — the sticky allocation, is that something we can control from our side or do you need Redwood to change it?
[03:12] Jules: good question — currently it's a Redwood routing policy which we can toggle per-customer. for the canary we'll enable it in the Dedicated pool config and give you the toggle in the console.

[03:30] Priya: the canary plan sounds good — what's the expected latency delta with sticky allocation?
[03:36] Jules: based on our internal tests with similar workloads, tail latency improves ~25-40% for long-context requests because we avoid cold KV misses; average p50 is generally unchanged. i'll share the test vectors in the doc.
[03:50] Diego: can you also share the exact autoscaler diff? we need to compare with our cluster autoscaler rules.
[03:56] Jules: yep i'll attach the diff and the recommended policy (we bumped cooldown and increased minimum pods to reduce churn).

[04:08] Samir: on long-term reliability improvements we proposed in the doc: smarter batching heuristics to reduce simultaneous eviction workload, better routing that factors in sequence length, and a new SLO dashboard that explicitly shows kv-miss rates, cache hit ratio, and allocation churn.
[04:30] Maya: those dashboards will be important — our oncall team needs clear thresholds for when to page.
[04:36] Ava: agreed; we'll add SLOs in the Redwood Console and set a default alert at 5% for cache evictions per minute and a separate alert for autoscaler churn. we can customize the thresholds for Lyra.

[04:54] Ethan: quick security question — the audit logs during the mitigation were forwarded to our SIEM, correct?
[04:59] Samir: yes we enabled forwarding and the logs show the config changes. we'll include the log excerpt in the postmortem doc link.

[05:10] Maya: i wanted to ask about the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff — we were using Hosted for this workload; is Dedicated the recommended path to avoid this kind of ephemeral churn?
[05:20] Jules: Dedicated helps because it reduces multi-tenant scheduling noise and gives you pinned capacity, but it doesn't eliminate cache eviction issues if a workload has spikes with many long-context requests. the combined approach is to run critical ingestion on Dedicated with sticky allocation and leave less critical, bursty traffic on Hosted.
[05:38] Priya: procurement may need a 30-45 day lead time for reserved capacity. we'll flag that.

[05:46] Diego: on the canary steps — we'll route 20% of traffic to the Dedicated pool with sticky allocation for 72 hours, run the same synthetic load that triggered the incident, and capture p50/p95/p99 and cache metrics.
[05:58] Jules: and Redwood will provide the synthetic script and the runbook. we also recommend running a shadow mode first so we can measure without impacting users.

[06:12] Maya: can you also include the mitigation for function/tool-calls? some of our requests use the tool-calling pattern and we saw increased attachments to external tools during the outage.
[06:22] Jules: yes we'll add guidance — rate limit tool calls and enable local caching on tool results. there was a mis-transcription in the doc where 'tool calling' was written as 'tooth calling' — we fixed that.

[06:40] Samir: ok let's go through the action items quickly and owners — Samir will send the postmortem doc; Jules will send autoscaler diffs and synthetic script; Ava will provision SLO dashboards and alerts; Diego will run canary; Priya will confirm procurement. any objections?
[06:58] Priya: sounds good, timeline fits.
[07:02] Ethan: security is good with the current plan, please include audit log pointers.

[07:10] Maya: one last ask — can you include a short blameless sentence in the doc for leadership? we need a single-paragraph summary for execs.
[07:18] Samir: yes we'll include an executive blameless summary and the key metrics.

[07:25] Samir: ok next steps and we'll schedule a 2-week follow-up — proposed March 30th at 14:00 UTC, but we'll send a calendar invite.
[07:34] Maya: thanks everyone. appreciate the quick response.
[07:38] Jules: thanks, ttyl.

End of transcript.
